title: About
text:
This project combines historical and real-time financial data with AI to produce automated research reports for US growth stock investors. By feeding macroeconomic indicators, equity market data, and commodity prices into an AI model, each report identifies historical patterns, draws parallels to current conditions, and highlights risks and opportunities for growth-oriented portfolios.
All charts and visualizations in the reports are created by the author — the AI generates only the written analysis.

Data Sources
Every report is grounded in real data from:

FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data): Inflation (CPI), GDP growth, unemployment, Fed balance sheet, Treasury yields, household debt, recession indicators, Fed funds rate, and high-yield credit spreads
Yahoo Finance: MSCI World Index, S&P 500, NASDAQ 100, Dow Jones, VIX, gold, and Brent crude oil
Multpl.com: S&P 500 trailing P/E ratios

title: Market Research
text:
Over the past three months, global markets have been defined by a severe energy shock and a resurgence of inflation, with Brent crude surging past $100 per barrel to $102.70 as of October 2026 amid escalating Middle Eastern geopolitical tensions. This macroeconomic headwind pushed global sovereign yields to multi-decade highs, with the US 10-year Treasury reaching 5.24% and the 30-year breaching 5.60% by early October 2026. Despite this, global equities have shown surprising resilience, with the MSCI World Index hovering near 4,926 as of October 2026, driven largely by a rotation back into mega-cap tech and an earnings supercycle that has kept valuation multiples in check. Gold has also skyrocketed to $4,172 per ounce as of October 2026, reflecting a classic late-cycle flight to safety and inflation hedging reminiscent of the late 1970s.
The divergence between global macroeconomic stress and equity market performance is stark when we isolate the US market’s reaction to these compounding pressures.



MSCI World Equity Index


The current environment forces a comparison to two distinct historical boom-and-bust cycles: the 1973-1974 oil shock and the 1999-2000 tech divergence. On the macroeconomic front, headline CPI sits at 3.4% as of August 2026, while core CPI is 2.4%. The Federal Reserve’s decision to hike the target rate to 4.0% as of September 2026 mirrors the late 1970s stop-go policy, where energy-driven inflation forced the central bank’s hand, ultimately stifling rate-sensitive growth equities. The catalyst this time is Brent crude, which has retraced its multi-year consolidation to hit $102.70 as of October 2026, acting as a regressive tax on the consumer and reigniting the inflation premium in long-term bonds.



Brent Oil Prices


This energy shock has fundamentally altered the risk-free rate, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.24% and the 2-year to 4.78% as of October 2026. The resulting yield curve dynamics and the surge in the long end echo the 1994 bond market rout and the tightening cycle of 2000, where the cost of capital began to ruthlessly discount long-duration cash flows. Meanwhile, the ICE BofA High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread has widened to 3.24% as of October 2026, signaling that credit markets are beginning to price in the stress of higher borrowing costs on levered corporates. However, household debt service payments remain a contained 11.11% of disposable income as of the second quarter of 2026, which is notably less fragile than the 15.84% peak observed prior to the 2008 financial crisis.



US 2Y and 10Y Treasury Yields and Spread


Despite the rising discount rate, the S&P 500 closed at 7,722 as of October 2026 with a trailing P/E of 26.34. What is fascinating is the bifurcation under the surface. The Nasdaq 100 has surged to 30,807 as of October 2026, heavily supported by a rotation from semiconductor hardware suppliers toward the hyperscalers and software companies that are actually monetizing the AI buildout. This concentration of market cap and earnings growth among a handful of cash-flowing monopolies closely resembles the late-stage 1999 market, where the broader index masked the underlying damage being done by rising yields to the long tail of unprofitable growth names.



Performance of Major US Stock Indices


While the headline index appears resilient, the trailing P/E of 26.34 as of October 2026 masks a severe compression in forward multiples for the broader market, as earnings revisions have outpaced price appreciation. We are witnessing a market that is pricing in a permanent structural shift in the cost of capital, rewarding only those growth companies with immediate, self-funding free cash flow.



S&P 500 PE Ratio


When evaluating the current landscape for US growth equities, we must confront several distinct risks: * The 10-year Treasury yield at 5.24% as of October 2026 acts as a gravity well for long-duration, unprofitable growth equities, echoing the 2000 tightening cycle where the discount rate systematically destroyed the present value of distant cash flows. * Geopolitical tail risk keeping Brent crude above $100 as of October 2026 acts as a regressive tax on the consumer and forces the Fed to maintain a restrictive 4.0% target rate as of September 2026, crushing multiple expansion for the broader market.
Conversely, this environment presents specific opportunities for the disciplined investor: * The rotation toward AI hyperscalers and software companies offers a distinct opportunity, as these entities are generating the free cash flow necessary to self-fund their capital expenditures without relying on the expensive 5.24% credit market. * Energy and commodity-linked equities are direct beneficiaries of the structural repricing of geopolitical risk and the $102.70 Brent crude floor as of October 2026, providing a natural hedge against the inflationary pressures that are punishing traditional tech multiples.
Given this highly bifurcated market, my suggested portfolio exposure is: * 50-75% allocation to US growth stocks. The market is severely split; while speculative, long-duration growth is being crushed by the 5.24% 10-year yield as of October 2026, cash-flowing tech monopolies are successfully passing through costs and pricing in the new macro reality, warranting a substantial but not fully aggressive allocation.
